label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: volcano
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (10 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 11 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano 3,776 meters tall
- Stratovolcanoes are built of alternating layers of lava flows and ash
- Gas dissolved in magma expands as it rises and drives explosive eruptions

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: the chamber glows red-hot and magma rises up the crack. actions: dig dig; magma show; magma melt (on "melt"); magma rise (on "rise")
   idea: rock melts deep underground and rises up a crack
   cue words: "melt", "rise"
2. problem
   on screen: gas bubbles rise in the chamber and a pressure gauge fills into the red. actions: bubbles show (on "bubbles"); stand show (on "pressure"); pressure show (on "pressure"); pressure count (on "pressure")
   idea: gas bubbles in the magma build up pressure
   cue words: "bubbles", "pressure"
   its fact: Gas dissolved in magma expands as it rises and drives explosive eruptions
3. stakes
   on screen: a blast bursts from the vent, smoke rises and ash falls. actions: pressure hide (on "blasts"); bubbles hide (on "blasts"); blast go (on "blasts"); smoke start (on "ash"); ash start (on "ash")
   idea: it blasts out and throws ash into the sky
   cue words: "blasts", "ash"
4. fix1
   on screen: a cone of rock appears and orange lava pours down it. actions: volcano show (on "lava"); volcano cone (on "lava"); volcano glow (on "lava"); volcano pour (on "pours")
   idea: lava pours down and cools into a cone of rock
   cue words: "lava", "pours"
5. problem2
   on screen: another blast and a second darker layer of rock on top of the cone. actions: blast go (on "eruption"); volcano layer (on "layer")
   idea: the next eruption buries the cone under another layer
   cue words: "eruption", "layer"
6. name
   on screen: an outline traces the volcano. actions: volcano outline show (on "stratovolcano")
   idea: this is a stratovolcano
   cue words: "stratovolcano"
7. how
   on screen: arrows point at the stacked rock layers of the cone. actions: volcano outline hide (on "Layers"); layer arrows show (on "Layers")
   idea: layers of lava and ash stack up one on another
   cue words: "Layers"
   its fact: Stratovolcanoes are built of alternating layers of lava flows and ash
8. fact
   on screen: a meters counter beside the cone ticks up to 3,776. actions: layer arrows hide (on "Fuji"); stand 2 show (on "Fuji"); height show (on "Fuji"); height count (on "3776")
   idea: Mount Fuji grew this way to 3,776 meters
   cue words: "Fuji", "3776"
   its fact: Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano 3,776 meters tall
9. finish
   on screen: snow appears on the peak and a ring of rocks round the base, the ash stops. actions: ash stop (on "Add"); smoke stop (on "Add"); light clear (on "Add"); volcano pourBack (on "Add"); volcano snow (on "snow"); rocks show (on "rocks"); height hide (on "Add")
   idea: snow on the peak and a ring of rocks round its base
   cue words: "Add", "snow", "rocks"
10. congrats
   on screen: the calm snowy volcano with trees
   idea: you have built a volcano
   cue words: (none)
